title: Relay Tower
summary: Point a dish at the value of an inverse trigonometric expression: principal branches, sums of angles and substitution identities.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 2.3, Properties of inverse trigonometric functions
concepts: sin⁻¹(sin x) and cos⁻¹(cos x) outside the branch
learningOutcome: The student can bring an angle into the principal branch, add inverse trigonometric angles with a tangent formula, and simplify an expression by a trigonometric substitution.

levels.title: Back into the branch
levels.adds: Baseline: sin⁻¹(sin x) = x only when x is in [−π/2, π/2]; otherwise find the angle in the branch with the same sine (Ex 2.2 Q10, Q11; Misc Q1, Q2; Example 6).
hints: Check whether x is in the principal branch of the outer function.
If not, use an identity such as sin(π − x) = sin x to find an angle in the branch.
The value is that angle, not x.

levels.title: Adding angles
levels.adds: New: the sum of two inverse functions, using tan(A + B), sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2, and the branch of the result (Ex 2.2 Q12; Misc Q3 to Q7).
hints: Take the tangent of the whole sum with tan(A + B).
A tangent of 1 means π/4 and −1 means 3π/4 or −π/4: which fits the size of the angles?
sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x is π/2 for any x.

levels.title: Substitution
levels.adds: New: simplify by putting x = tan θ, sin θ or cos θ, then use double and triple angle identities (Ex 2.2 Q1 to Q7; Examples 3 to 5).
hints: Choose the substitution that matches the shape under the root or the fraction.
Simplify with a double or triple angle formula to get a multiple of θ.
Put θ back as an inverse function of x and evaluate at the given x.

misconceptions: sin⁻¹(sin x) = x for every x
cos⁻¹ has the same range as sin⁻¹
